Generate exactly 20 realistic web filenames to discover api documentation.

The goal is to discover valid web resources.

Use the score feedback from the previous result to improve the next filename list.

Scoring rules:

* +1 point when a filename returns HTTP status 200.
* -2 points when a filename duplicates any filename generated previously.
* Avoid all previously generated filenames.
* Do not repeat unsuccessful filename patterns unless there is a strong reason to vary them.
* Maximise the total score while keeping the filenames realistic and diverse.

Each item must be a single filename only.

Think of filenames or endpoint names that a web application developer would realistically create.

Prefer names that are commonly found in production applications.

Examples:

swagger
swagger-ui
api-doc
logout
login
signin
register
phpinfo.php
dashboard
profile
account
settings
index.html
app.js
Web.config
admin
health
status
metrics
robots.txt
config
search
upload.aspx
download
export
import
help.php
contact
sitemap.xml
manifest.json

The user may provide feedback in this format:

Last score: <score>
Score breakdown:
<score_lines>

Return ONLY valid JSON in this exact format:

{
  "items": [
    "logout",
    "login"
  ]
}

Requirements:

* The "items" array must contain exactly 20 filenames.
* Every filename must be unique.
* Every item must be a single filename or endpoint name.
* Prefer names between 1 and 25 characters (excluding the extension).
* Use at most one file extension.
* Use only letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores and a single period before the extension.
* Prefer short, memorable names that a developer would actually choose.
* Generate names that could realistically exist in a production web application.
* Avoid automatically generated, keyword-stuffed or descriptive names.
* Do not invent extremely long filenames.
* Do not concatenate multiple words or concepts together to create oversized names.
* Do not use markdown.
* Do not wrap the JSON in code fences.
* Do not include explanations or any text outside the JSON.
